title: Saint Kitts
capsule: Saint Kitts and Nevis is a two-island federation in the eastern Caribbean, achieving associated statehood with the United Kingdom in 1967 and full independence on 19 September 1983 as the smallest sovereign state in the Western Hemisphere by both area and population. The sugar industry, which had shaped the colonial economy since the 17th century, was formally closed in 2005 after decades of decline, and the economy shifted to tourism and financial services. The federation has been marked by recurring debates over Nevisian secession; a 1998 referendum on Nevis independence failed to achieve the required two-thirds majority, obtaining 61.8% support. It remains a Commonwealth realm with the British monarch as head of state.
